architecture_principles: the unit of decision is an experiment, not a formulation
value of information is computed by a deterministic scientific tool, not by an additional language model
every registered hypothesis carries an explicit pre-result prediction rule and an explicit falsification condition
a measurement that cannot separate any registered hypothesis scores zero discrimination, and that is a scientific result rather than a defect
weight sensitivity is reported as decision stability, never as model confidence
ties in the deterministic layer are reported as ties; the tool must not manufacture a preference it does not have
held-out result data are structurally removed before any payload is assembled
the mechanism question and the Agent framework are separate contributions and are reported separately

candidate_space.rationale: V4 deliberately reuses the byte-identical V3 lattice. Continuous-space optimization and any new wet-lab work are out of scope, so that the measured change between V3 and V4 is the decision object and the VOI layer, not the search space.

architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> evidence/tool layer (including the deterministic VOI tool) -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze
architecture.claim_boundary: V4.0.0 selects an experiment from pre-result evidence under an outcome-blind runtime. Its adjudication tests whether a registered hypothesis survives contact with the completed measurement. It is not a contemporaneous pre-experimental record and does not claim that the historical decision used this ranking.
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_VOI_GUIDED_EXPERIMENT_SELECTION_AGENT_V4
non_goals: adding a language model to compute value of information
adding Agent roles beyond planner, tools, proposer, skeptic, robustness adjudicator, judge and freeze
turning the study into a pure AI benchmark
weakening or replacing the rheological mechanism result
architecture.purpose: Outcome-blind scientific decision Agent that selects the next formulation x measurement EXPERIMENT by transparent value of information, rather than selecting a formulation candidate alone.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode and the scientific question that the next experiment must answer, then request the evidence needed to judge experiments rather than formulations

execute read-only scientific tools, including the paper-derived state-aware rheology tool, external evidence retrieval, and the deterministic VOI tool that scores every formulation x measurement experiment card
propose the experiment with the highest scientific information value, stating the hypotheses it separates and what each possible outcome would establish
attack the proposed experiment on hypothesis coverage, confounding, interpretability of the primary observable, and whether the stated falsification criterion can actually be met by the measurement
adjudicate whether the proposed experiment survives the reported VOI weight sensitivity and the skeptic's strongest objection
commit to one experiment card, or abstain, and state the acceptance and falsification criteria that will adjudicate it
programmatically validate and freeze the experiment card with timestamps, model identifiers and cryptographic hashes of every input

architecture.supersedes_nothing: V4 is an independent architecture. configs/agent_v3.json, prompts/agent_v3_*.txt, src/pur_new/agent_v3.py and every frozen V3 run record remain unchanged and are not reinterpreted by V4.

voi_tool.explicitly_not: distance to any held-out formulation. No target coordinate enters any component, weight or tie-break.
voi_tool.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk
voi_tool.name: score_experiment_cards
voi_tool.not_a_posterior: The local design contains six audited realizations and two thermal-hold trajectories. That does not support a calibrated Bayesian expected-information computation, so no posterior probability is fabricated. Weight sensitivity is reported instead.

decision_stability_sent_to_model.metric_is_not: model confidence; posterior probability; calibrated expected information
decision_stability_sent_to_model.tie_interpretation: The deterministic VOI layer is indifferent among the tied top experiments: they share an identical component vector. Tie-breaking is therefore a genuine task left to the Agent, and any selection inside this set cannot have been read off the VOI ranking.
decision_stability_sent_to_model.voi_formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.

evidence_policy.description: For prospective/blind Agent evaluation. The Agent may see original-system measurements and external analogue evidence, but not the target validation formulation identity, its wet-lab outcome, or any outcome-derived labels.

judge_normalized.acceptance_criterion: Accept low-drift dual-axis performance if every valid independent repeat, with at least two repeats, has SI_15_60 < 3.57%. This is below half of the preregistered 7.13% linear-dilution prediction and supports the shared low-drift prediction of H-RESIN and H-DUAL over H-CORE.
judge_normalized.falsification_criterion: If every valid independent repeat, with at least two repeats, has SI_15_60 < 3.57%, falsify H-CORE. If every valid independent repeat has SI_15_60 >= 7.13%, falsify H-RESIN; this outcome conflicts with, but does not definitively falsify, H-DUAL. Results from 3.57% through <7.13%, or repeats falling into different decision regions, falsify neither hypothesis decisively.
judge_normalized.next_experiment_if_falsified: Run a preparation-blocked M-HOLD-120 panel containing an acrylic-only formulation at comparable reactive mass fraction and a concurrent unmodified E2-core control, using at least three independent preparations per arm and retaining eta_15 and the full 15, 30, 45, and 60 min trajectories.
judge_normalized.primary_observable: Repeat-level SI_15_60 = 100 * (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15 at 120 C, reported as percent for each of at least two independent preparations.
judge_normalized.rationale: This card directly measures the declared 120 C hold-drift failure mode, tests whether S1C51 reaches a practically low-drift regime, and provides a numerically resolvable H-CORE versus superlinear-suppression contrast. It is not a molecular-mechanism test and cannot distinguish general resin suppression from tackifier-required suppression.
judge_normalized.stage_disagreements_resolved: I followed the Proposer and Robustness Adjudicator on selecting S1C51::M-HOLD-120: it is in the stable tied top set, uses the strongest supplied loading anchors, and avoids the larger 22.5-25% acrylic perturbations. I followed the Skeptic on interpretation: this single dual-axis card cannot separate H-RESIN from H-DUAL or uniquely attribute suppression to either modifier axis, and the E1-to-E2 baseline transfer is confounded. The Robustness Adjudicator preferred expanding the card into a matched panel, but no selectable identifier for that panel or its required balanced acrylic-only arm is supplied; therefore I commit the identified anchor and make the panel the required follow-up rather than silently treating it as part of this card.

uncertainty_decomposition.evidence_coverage_uncertainty: Moderate: 20% acrylic-like and 5% tackifier-like loadings lie within the supplied supported regions, but the external-prior queries returned no rows and the evidence consists of analogues rather than direct local hold measurements.
uncertainty_decomposition.extrapolation_uncertainty: Low for modifier loading because both axes are inside the stated supported regions, but substantial for transferring the E1-derived 9.51% baseline to the E2-based reactive core, which differs in composition and NCO:OH ratio.
uncertainty_decomposition.measurement_uncertainty: The registered drift-resolution threshold is 2.0 percentage points. SI_15_60 is directly observed without fitting or extrapolation, but repeat discordance would be inconclusive rather than pooled post hoc.
uncertainty_decomposition.realization_state_uncertainty: High: M-HOLD-120 does not control process state, six process fields are missing, and E2 showed a 3.5688-fold viscosity spread at 120 C. Independent preparations, recorded histories, eta_15, and complete trajectories are therefore required.

planner.failure_mode: Viscosity growth during prolonged isothermal melt residence at 120 C (thermal-hold drift), with substantial formulation dependence.
planner.failure_mode_evidence: The original E5 thermal-hold run increased by 51.54% from 15 to 60 min and by 93.08% from 15 to 90 min at 120 C, compared with 9.51% and 16.85%, respectively, for E1. These direct matched-window observations establish thermal-hold drift as the dominant unresolved failure mode.
planner.least_resolved_justification: Only E1 and E5 have local 120 C hold trajectories, each represented by one listed run over 15-90 min, while no hold trajectory is available for E2 or any candidate composition. In contrast, temperature response is measured over 80-130 C for multiple formulations and runs, and realized viscosity levels are repeatedly observed despite large E2 between-run spread. Therefore the candidate compositions' time-dependent viscosity growth is the least constrained coordinate.
measurement_requirements: Use the registered matched-window 120 C hold protocol: measure viscosity at 15, 30, 45, and 60 min and report SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15 as a percentage.
Run at least two independent preparations per tested composition and fully record preparation and residence histories so formulation effects are not conflated with realization-state variation.

Test a contrast that includes an acrylic-only composition and a composition with a nonzero minor tackifier-like fraction at comparable reactive mass fraction; this is required to distinguish H-DUAL from H-RESIN.
For each tested composition, preregister the H-CORE prediction E1_drift times reactive mass fraction and the H-RESIN threshold of less than half that linear-dilution prediction.
Use the registered 2 percentage-point drift-resolution threshold and do not treat predictions closer than that threshold as mechanistically separable.
Retain the individual viscosity values and full time trajectories, not only the final drift statistic, to detect nonmonotonic or otherwise non-comparable hold behavior.

Measure or calibrate the realized viscosity level for each preparation at a temperature within local measured support so unusually low or high starting state can be separated from true relative drift suppression.
Preserve the source viscosity unit as unknown unless established by source-level evidence; hypothesis adjudication should rely on the dimensionless matched-window drift.
planner.scientific_question: At matched reactive mass fraction and controlled preparation state, is the 120 C viscosity drift from 15 to 60 min consistent with reactive-core linear dilution, suppressed substantially beyond linear dilution by resin modification, or suppressed only when the minor tackifier-like axis is nonzero rather than by acrylic-like modification alone?

hypotheses_not_separated: H-RESIN vs H-DUAL; both predict approximately 3.57% drift at this dual-axis composition, so an acrylic-only hold experiment is required to separate them

outcome_interpretation.if_acceptance_criterion_met: Drift below 3.57% across at least two repeats is less than half the 7.13% linear-dilution prediction. This falsifies H-CORE and establishes superlinear suppression at this dual-axis composition, but it supports the shared low-drift predictions of H-RESIN and H-DUAL without distinguishing between them.
outcome_interpretation.if_falsification_criterion_met: Drift at or above 7.13% falsifies H-RESIN and supports H-CORE over the registered low-drift alternatives. It also conflicts with H-DUAL's predicted low drift when tackifier is present, although the registry's definitive H-DUAL falsifier remains low drift in an acrylic-only composition.
outcome_interpretation.if_intermediate: Drift from 3.57% to below 7.13% indicates partial or borderline suppression and does not meet either decisive card criterion. Values within the 2 percentage-point measurement resolution of 7.13% remain compatible with H-CORE, while repeat disagreement or unusual starting viscosity would indicate unresolved realization-state effects.

proposer.primary_observable: SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15, percent, measured directly during the 120 C hold

ranked_alternatives.why_lower_value: It has the same deterministic VOI and remains inside the supported region with lower modifier burden, but 17.5% acrylic is less directly anchored than the repeated approximately 19-20% external examples.
It has the smallest modifier burden, but its 15% acrylic level is supported only as a directional lower-region point whose literature fraction denominator remains unverified.
It has identical discrimination and directness but uses 22.5% acrylic, outside the conservative initial 15-20% test band and with a larger departure from the characterized local chemistry.
Although 25% acrylic is directly supported, it is the largest tied perturbation and lies at the upper edge of the broad supported region without adding hypothesis separation.

proposer.reasoning: The matched-window hold directly measures the unresolved failure coordinate without model fitting and separates two of the three registered hypothesis pairs. S1C51 is fully inside supported intervention regions, uses the strongest combined external anchors, and avoids unnecessary modifier burden relative to the higher-acrylic tied cards. At least two independently prepared repeats and recorded preparation/residence histories are essential because process-state risk remains moderate.
proposer.tie_break_justification: S1C51 combines 20% acrylic-like modifier, directly supported by repeated approximately 19-20% external examples, with 5% minor tackifier-like modifier, inside the repeatedly documented 4.8-6.4% cluster. It therefore has stronger direct intervention support than the 15% point with a provisional denominator, while avoiding the larger perturbations of 22.5-25% acrylic. The observable and hypothesis discrimination are otherwise identical across the tied set.

robustness_adjudication.change_from_proposal: Retain S1C51::M-HOLD-120 as the preferred dual-axis anchor, but do not run or interpret it as a standalone experiment. Expand it into a preregistered, preparation-blocked matched panel containing S1C51, an acrylic-only arm at comparable reactive mass fraction, and a concurrent unmodified E2-core control. Use at least three independent preparations per arm, record eta_15 and full preparation/residence histories, and preregister replicate aggregation, discordance, and abnormal-starting-viscosity rules. No supplied identifier uniquely names the required acrylic-only balanced arm or the complete panel, so S1C51::M-HOLD-120 identifies the retained anchor rather than the whole revised design.
residual_decision_risk: The required acrylic-only arm with matched reactive fraction may require a verified inert balancing component; its chemical inertness and compatibility are not established in the payload.
M-HOLD-120 does not itself control process state, and the observed E2 viscosity spread at 120 C is 3.5688-fold, so realization-state variation may still obscure formulation effects.

The E1-derived H-CORE prediction is not a concurrent E2-core baseline and differs in NCO:OH ratio and core composition; without the added E2 control, deviation from linear dilution is not uniquely attributable to modifiers.
Replicate aggregation, threshold discordance, and handling of unusual eta_15 values must be preregistered to avoid post hoc adjudication.
Even the revised rheological panel can support formulation-level suppression or tackifier dependence, not a molecularly resolved encounter-frequency mechanism.
The reported decision stability covers only one-at-a-time weight multipliers from 0.5 to 1.5; untested joint or more-extreme perturbations remain outside the assessment.
The deterministic score does not encode the decisive value of separating H-RESIN from H-DUAL, which is why all five tied top experiments remain scientifically incomplete when run alone.
robustness_adjudication.skeptic_objection_reasoning: The objection changes the design rather than merely limiting interpretation. Every member of the deterministic tied top set is a dual-axis formulation for which H-RESIN and H-DUAL make identical predictions, so choosing another tied member would preserve the same hypothesis entanglement. The stated three-way question and the planner's requirements therefore call for a matched panel, not S1C51 alone: retain S1C51 as the supported dual-axis arm, add an acrylic-only arm at comparable reactive mass fraction, and add a concurrent E2-based unmodified reactive-core control. The acrylic-only contrast is required to test whether low drift requires the minor tackifier axis, while the concurrent core control addresses the mismatch between the E1-derived linear-dilution baseline and S1C51's E2 core. Thus the direct M-HOLD-120 observable remains appropriate, but a single S1C51 result would only establish a dual-axis formulation-level effect and could not answer the three-way question.
robustness_adjudication.weight_sensitivity_assessment: S1C51::M-HOLD-120 remains within the unchanged five-experiment tied top set in all 25 reported one-term perturbation scenarios. Scaling any individual weight from 0.5 to 1.5 times its base value produced no recommendation flip; every recommendation_flip_boundary therefore survives the entire sweep. No tested weighting, defensible or otherwise, makes the proposal cease to be top ranked. This conclusion is limited to the reported sweep: the margin to the first strictly lower experiment is only 0.004583, and untested joint or more-extreme re-weightings could change the ranking.

skeptic.falsification_criterion_assessment: M-HOLD-120 can directly produce SI_15_60 values below 3.57% or at/above 7.13%, so the stated H-CORE and H-RESIN numerical criteria are attainable, and their 3.5662-point separation exceeds the declared 2.0-point resolution. The protocol cannot, however, attain the registry's definitive H-DUAL falsifier because no acrylic-only composition is tested. A repeat-level aggregation or discordance rule should also be preregistered.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The experiment cannot answer the stated three-way scientific question or determine whether suppression is a general resin effect or specifically requires the minor tackifier axis.
objections.objection: The proposed experiment tests only S1C51, which contains 20.0% acrylic-like modifier and 5.0% minor tackifier-like modifier. H-RESIN and H-DUAL both predict 3.5663% drift for this composition, so their predicted difference is 0 percentage points, below the declared 2.0 percentage-point resolution. This also violates the planner's explicit measurement requirement to include both an acrylic-only composition and a composition with nonzero minor tackifier at comparable reactive mass fraction. The Proposer correctly lists this pair under hypotheses_not_separated.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A result at or above 7.13% could be overstated as falsifying H-DUAL even though the registered decisive acrylic-only test was not performed.
objections.objection: The claimed separation 'H-CORE vs H-DUAL' is weaker than stated. The numerical predictions differ by 3.5662 percentage points, which exceeds the 2.0-point resolution, but the registry defines the definitive H-DUAL falsifier as low drift in an acrylic-only composition. S1C51 is dual-axis, so even high drift does not execute that registered falsification test; the Proposer acknowledges only that high drift would 'conflict with' H-DUAL.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A low-drift result would support only a dual-axis formulation-level effect; modifier-specific mechanism attribution would be unsupported.
objections.objection: S1C51 activates both modifier axes simultaneously: AC1920 changes from 0 to 20.0 wt% and TK100 changes from 0 to 5.0 wt%, while reactive material falls to 0.7500 mass fraction. Therefore any drift suppression cannot be attributed separately to the acrylic-like modifier, the minor tackifier-like modifier, or their interaction. In particular, the proposed hold cannot establish the H-DUAL attribution that acrylic principally relocates viscosity while tackifier is required for drift suppression.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Falsification of the empirical E1-based linear-dilution rule could be misinterpreted as evidence that the modifiers caused suppression.
objections.objection: The 7.13% H-CORE prediction uses the single E1 hold result, 9.51%, multiplied by S1C51's reactive fraction of 0.75, but S1C51 preserves the E2 reactive core at NCO:OH 1.80 whereas E1 has NCO:OH 1.70 and different MDI/polyol fractions. No E2-core thermal-hold trajectory or concurrent unmodified reactive-core control is included. Thus deviation from 7.13% can reflect reactive-core or stoichiometric differences from E1 rather than resin-induced superlinear suppression.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Preparation-state variation could be mistaken for a formulation effect, especially with only two repeats.
objections.objection: M-HOLD-120 is explicitly marked controls_process_state=false, with process_state_risk 0.75 and six missing process fields. The proposal requires at least two preparations and recorded histories, but it does not include a concurrent matched control or a preregistered rule for excluding or stratifying preparations with unusual eta_15. This matters because E2 showed a 3.5688-fold max/min viscosity spread at 120 C.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: None for direct readout; interpretation is limited mainly by the design confounds rather than by observable construction.
objections.objection: No material interpretability defect is present for the primary observable. SI_15_60 is calculated directly from measured eta_15 and eta_60 values during the same 120 C hold; it requires no regression fit, extrapolation, or imputation. Retaining the 30 and 45 min values also permits inspection for nonmonotonic behavior.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The experiment may be presented as capable of falsifying all registered alternatives even though only the H-CORE/H-RESIN numerical contrast is operationally testable, and discordant repeats may be adjudicated post hoc.
objections.objection: The numerical H-CORE and H-RESIN criteria are practically attainable because the protocol directly measures drift and their S1C51 predictions differ by 3.5662 percentage points, exceeding the 2.0-point resolution. However, the protocol cannot attain H-DUAL's registered falsification criterion because that criterion requires an acrylic-only composition, which is absent. In addition, 'across at least two repeats' does not specify adjudication when one repeat is below and one above a threshold.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: If the encounter-frequency explanation were asserted as established, it would exceed what the planned viscosity measurement can demonstrate.
objections.objection: No direct outcome leakage is evident in the supplied proposal: the target hold result and validation identity are excluded, and the tie-break uses stated external analogue regions rather than an unmeasured outcome. The rheological hold can establish only formulation-level suppression, not the H-RESIN statement's molecular explanation involving reduced encounter frequency. The registry and Proposer largely respect this boundary by claiming superlinear suppression rather than a molecularly resolved pathway.

skeptic.recommended_change: Replace the single-composition experiment with a preregistered matched panel run under the same preparation blocks: S1C51, an acrylic-only formulation at comparable reactive mass fraction, and a concurrent unmodified reactive-core control based on E2. For clean tackifier attribution, keep acrylic loading and reactive fraction fixed by replacing the 5% tackifier with a verified inert balancing component in the no-tackifier arm. Use at least three independent preparations per arm, record eta_15 as the realized-state anchor, and preregister how replicate disagreement and abnormal starting viscosity will be handled.
skeptic.strongest_objection: The single dual-axis S1C51 hold omits the required acrylic-only contrast. Because H-RESIN and H-DUAL have identical 3.5663% predictions at S1C51, the experiment cannot distinguish general resin suppression from tackifier-required suppression and therefore cannot answer the stated three-way scientific question.

tool_trace.name: get_state_aware_rheology_summary
tool_trace.reason: This must be obtained first to load the upstream material-state structure, shared thermal response, state-calibration evidence, and E1/E5 hold contrast before any candidate or experiment ranking is admissible.

claim_boundaries: The shared-shape/state-shift structure is established only within the measured local chemistry family.
The apparent E_eta descriptor is rheological, not a chemical reaction activation energy.
The E1/E5 hold contrast does not identify a unique molecular mechanism.
The phosphoric-acid-labelled E1 +P curve is not used in the chemistry-audited primary state model.
No validation-formulation identity or outcome is used by this tool.
design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.
When the failure mode is hot-hold drift, choose an experiment and measurement window that directly test drift rather than only matching one nominal viscosity value.
Use external resin/tackifier evidence to define chemically plausible directions, but do not convert analogue proximity into a predicted local outcome.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.
one_point_state_calibration.validation_scheme: leave one nominal formulation out; fit shared shape on the remaining formulations; use one anchor from the held formulation

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, a realization-specific viscosity-scale intercept plus a shared quadratic inverse-temperature response closes the data far better than a formulation-level intercept using the same thermal basis.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.hold_window: For the current local study, 120 C and the common 15-60 min window directly interrogate the observed instability while matching the available validation window.
experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.

provenance_audit.reason: The source record is phosphoric-acid-labelled and its additive identity/amount is not represented in formulations.csv; it is retained as sensitivity-only until chemistry is reconciled.

result.source_scope: original pre-validation local measurements with chemistry-comparability audit

acrylic_like_modifier_pct_total.interpretation: 20 and 25% are directly commensurate coarse anchors in the current curated record. The 15% grid level is retained as a lower-bound design point, but the literature denominator for the reported 15% addition level is not treated as an exact total-formulation anchor until reverified.

evidence: PAT_US5932680A: examples around 4.8-6.4% tackifying/hydrocarbon resin and preferred resin range 3-10 wt%
PAT_US20070155859A1: tackifiers/rheology-control agents typically used below about 10 wt%
minor_tackifier_like_modifier_pct_total.interpretation: 5% represents the repeatedly documented minor-resin region and 10% is a conservative coarse upper level.

result.claim_boundary: External examples are analogues. They support candidate-family and coarse-region hypotheses, not an exact optimum for AC1920/TK100 and not a proven local molecular mechanism. The current reconstruction uses only pre-result evidence at runtime; the exact validation coordinates and outcome are excluded from candidate construction, ranking and tie-breaking.

decision_policy.claim_boundary: This policy can recover an evidence-supported formulation neighborhood, but it is not a predictor of the exact wet-lab optimum.

acrylic_like.basis: 15% directional lower-region evidence plus directly commensurate ~19-20% examples; 25% remains directly supported but is a larger perturbation.

minor_tackifier_like.basis: Curated PUR examples repeatedly place tackifying/hydrocarbon resin near 5%, with broader guidance below about 10%.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

historical_status.interpretation: The prospective historical claim attaches to the Agent recommendation itself. The current coarse grid and fine-refinement software are later reproducible operationalizations of the evidence-constrained region and are not represented as the original contemporaneous freeze algorithm unless older provenance is recovered.

local_reactive_core_anchor.reason: E2 is the geometric centre of the original five-point local design: 50/50 PPG2000/PDP-70 and NCO:OH=1.80, centered between E1/E3 stoichiometric perturbations and E4/E5 composition perturbations.
local_reactive_core_anchor.stoichiometry_note: The E2 NCO:OH=1.80 label applies to the original reactive core. If a modifier contributes reactive OH or another NCO-reactive group, true stoichiometry must be recalculated from verified material specifications.

stability_hypotheses.H1_formulation_family: Partial replacement of the reactive-only formulation by an acrylic-like and/or minor tackifier-like resin can reduce hot-hold viscosity drift under matched process conditions.
stability_hypotheses.H2_functionality: At comparable acrylic loading, lower effective reactive-group density or lower-OH acrylic chemistry is expected to be more favorable for hot-hold viscosity stability than more highly reactive acrylic chemistry.
stability_hypotheses.H3_region: A useful candidate region is expected within the externally supported coarse space spanned by 15-25% acrylic-like modifier and 0-10% minor tackifier-like modifier, while preserving the relative E2 reactive-core proportions.

tool_trace.name: inspect_formulation
tool_trace.reason: E2 is the reactive-core anchor; its composition fractions are needed to calculate reactive mass fraction and construct transparent linear-dilution predictions.

tool_trace.name: inspect_formulation
tool_trace.reason: E1 supplies the least-drifting original reference, so its composition must be audited before using its measured drift as the H-CORE baseline.

tool_trace.name: inspect_formulation
tool_trace.reason: E5 supplies the observed high-drift reference; its chemistry-axis fractions are needed to interpret the local contrast without conflating composition and process state.

tool_trace.name: get_hold_stability
tool_trace.reason: The complete measured E1 trajectory and deterministic matched-window descriptors are needed to freeze the original low-drift reference used by the registered hypotheses.

tool_trace.name: get_hold_stability
tool_trace.reason: The complete measured E5 trajectory is needed to characterize the high-drift failure reference over exactly the same time window proposed for candidate testing.

tool_trace.name: get_repeatability_risk
tool_trace.reason: E2 shows nominal temperature-sweep CVs of about 0.46-0.58 and max/min ratios of about 2.80-3.57; the detailed spread is needed to design state controls that prevent realization uncertainty from dominating the experiment.

tool_trace.name: get_temperature_support
tool_trace.reason: Measured support is needed to choose any viscosity-level calibration temperature without extrapolation and to verify that the proposed 110-120 C state checks remain inside the local domain.

tool_trace.name: query_external_priors
tool_trace.reason: The supplied external digest contains no acrylic-like rows, so source-level analogue evidence and its limitations are needed before judging acrylic-axis experiment coverage.

tool_trace.name: query_external_priors
tool_trace.reason: The supplied external digest contains no minor-tackifier-like rows, so source-level evidence is needed to assess whether candidate contrasts on the tackifier axis are externally grounded or primarily uncertainty probes.

voi_sent_to_model.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.
voi_sent_to_model.tie_note: These experiments share an identical component vector. The deterministic tool is indifferent among them. Any choice within this set must be justified scientifically.

top_cards.acceptance_criterion: Matched 15-60 min drift at 120 C stays below 3.80% across at least two repeats, i.e. below half the linear-dilution prediction of 7.61% implied by a reactive mass fraction of 0.8000. This accepts H-RESIN over H-CORE.
top_cards.falsification_criterion: H-RESIN is falsified if matched 15-60 min drift is at or above the linear-dilution prediction of 7.61%. H-CORE is falsified if drift falls below 3.80%, a separation larger than the 2.00% resolution threshold. This composition carries both axes, so it cannot separate H-RESIN from H-DUAL; an acrylic-only hold is the follow-up required for that.

measurement_plan.name: matched-window 120 C thermal hold
measurement_plan.protocol: Hold the melt at 120 C. Record viscosity at 15, 30, 45 and 60 min. Report the 15-60 min matched-window relative change. Run at least two independent repeats.
